name: Jesse Ventura
role: Governor of Minnesota (1999-2003); former professional wrestler and actor
summary: As governor of Minnesota, Ventura pushed for a single-chamber legislature and vetoed new abortion restrictions. After leaving office he campaigned against a constitutional ban on same-sex marriage, criticized the Iraq invasion and post-September 11 restrictions on civil liberties, and advocated cannabis legalization.

notes: This pass checked the Minnesota legislative veto register, the administration’s Big Plan report, state addresses, campaign and later interview transcripts, and the local books, alongside local MediaSum transcripts. Searches on the widest uncertainty lines covered racial equality and integration, collective bargaining and income, nationalism and overseas bases, and industrial and environmental policy. The review also covered taxation and banking, elections and institutional reform, war and diplomacy, criminal justice and civil liberties, healthcare and welfare, religion and education, immigration and trade, urban growth and energy, and technology. Ventura’s early endorsement of domestic partnerships preceded his campaign against the same-sex marriage amendment. Historical citations to tertiary compilations are retained in the signed review history.
